title: Special Topics in Government and Politics; American Jewry, Israel, and U.S. Public Policy: Peoplehood, Politics, and Power
description:
Cross-listed with ISRL349O. Credit only granted for ISRL349O or GVPT368N.

The Jewish people have long maintained a unique sense of peoplehood, which for much of Jewish history coincided with powerlessness and political marginalization. The modern American Jewish experience has been unique in Jewish history largely due to the opportunity structure afforded by the American political system; and power, specifically the American Jewish community s ability to adapt and participate in the policy arena to maximize its preferred outcomes. This upper-division course examines these features of American Jewry and its relationship with Israel in therealm of US public policy by focusing on historical development and Jewish political thought; organizational and representative structures; and highlighting several case studies and thematic topics.
